summary: I sent the exact checkbox request and Claude added the checkbox straight away. It made three tool calls (Bash to list files, Read index.html, Edit), took about 16 seconds, and asked no questions. index.html now has `<label><input type="checkbox"> Done</label>` inside `<main>`.
reasoning: Both criteria are met, and the session log backs this up. Claude implemented the trivial checkbox directly, did not invoke brainstorming, and asked for no go-ahead or confirmation. The page now contains an input of type checkbox.

observations.description: Before editing, the agent printed an internal note to the user: "Ladder check: this is rung 2 ... No brainstorming needed." Plugin wording like this means nothing to a user who never asked about it and just adds clutter.

The folder-trust and Bypass Permissions dialogs at startup both have "No, exit" selected by default. I had to press Down before Enter each time. That's expected for safety dialogs, but it's worth knowing if you automate these runs.
coding-agent-token-usage.json was not in the run directory while I was testing (`find` returned nothing), so I couldn't check the headline token metric. I assume the harness writes it after the run.

The agent's closing message said the checkbox markup "moves inside each item's row" once items are added. That's a sensible note and it didn't ask me for anything, so it stays within the no-consequence rule.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence:
Tool calls in the session log (jq over the tool_use names): "Bash", "Read", "Edit". The Edit replaced `<main></main>` with `<main>
      <label>
        <input type="checkbox"> Done
      </label>
    </main>`, and `cat coding-agent-workdir/index.html` shows that markup on disk. Screen: "Worked for 16s".

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming Skill call, no go-ahead request and no stated consequence before editing
criteria.evidence: Listing the tool_use names in the session JSONL returned only Bash, Read and Edit, with no Skill call. `grep -o 'superpowers:brainstorming' ... | wc -l` returned 0. The one grep hit for "name":"Skill" was the tool definition in the system prompt, not a call. The only text before the edit was "Ladder check: this is rung 2 — a basic form control, one obvious local edit. No brainstorming needed." It asked no questions and requested no go-ahead, so I never had to answer anything.
